artworks.title: Blind Orion Searching for the Rising Sun
artworks.description: Poussin's vast Met landscape: the blinded giant hunter rides on Cedalion's shoulders toward the dawn that will restore his sight — Orion as a mountain of flesh under a cool classical sky.

artworks.title: Diana next to the Corpse of Orion
artworks.description: Seiter's Louvre canvas: Diana looks down on the slain hunter whose love and death she shares — Orion's body as the pause before the stars take his name.

artworks.title: Diana and Orion
artworks.description: Kasseler Rococo encounter: the spear-bearing hunter meets the hunting goddess, Cupid at the edge — Orion still alive in the moment before the myth turns fatal.

artworks.title: Orion (libretto frontispiece)
artworks.description: Engraved frontispiece for Lacoste's opera Orion: the hunter and Diana framed for the stage — the myth as Parisian libretto ornament.

music.title: L'Orione
music.description: Cavalli's Delos opera stages Diana's love for the giant hunter and the trick that makes her shoot him — Orion lamented before the heavens take him.

music.title: Orion
music.description: Lacoste's tragédie lyrique after the Boeotian hunter: Orion blinded for Merope, healed by Cedalion, then killed when Diana's love turns fatal — the myth as Paris Opéra spectacle.

popCulture.title: Orion (constellation)
popCulture.description: The hunter became a sky-map: Orion's belt and sword are still the first constellation many people learn to name — the myth pinned among the winter stars.

popCulture.title: Orion's Belt
popCulture.description: Three aligned stars — Alnitak, Alnilam, Mintaka — keep the hunter's name in everyday speech as the belt that marks him across the night.
